subject: Integration contract: optional streaming callback param and deprecation window
messages:
From: Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@acme-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: integration@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: API contract change for realtime callbacks - integration impact

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Acme's product team is excited about Redwood's streaming callbacks for realtime scoring. As we've started work on our SDK upgrade we ran into an integration blocker: our customers rely on a deterministic callback_id field to correlate asynchronous events across our pipeline. The current Redwood streaming callback payload does not include a stable callback_id (it exposes request_id and partial_token indexes), and our client-side SDK needs an explicit, consumable field.

We propose adding an optional top-level field "callback_id" to the streaming token payloads (string, client-generated or server-echoed) and to the SDK event handler signature: onToken({token, callback_id, metadata}). This would be backwards-compatible if the field is optional, but we need clarity on the SDK/HTTP contract and the deprecation policy in case Redwood plans changes to the streaming payload surface.

Attached is a short proposal and a compatibility matrix showing how our releases would map to Redwood's semver. Can we get alignment on: 
- Whether Redwood is willing to accept an optional callback_id in the short term
- If yes, the expected timeline to ship it in hosted API and SDK (approx. release quarters)
- Redwood's long-term deprecation/major-version timeline for streaming payload changes

We'd like to keep our roadmap on track (we're targeting our SDK 3.0 stable in Q1) and would prefer at least a six-month deprecation window for any breaking changes. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Carlos
Lead Product Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-sdk-proposal.pdf (2 pages), compat-matrix.csv (spreadsheet)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: API contract change for realtime callbacks - integration impact

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. I reviewed the proposal and passed your compat matrix to Aditya (runtime) and Lauren (partner engineering). High level: adding an optional callback_id sounds reasonable as an additive change, but we need to confirm how it behaves for cached responses and whether it is stable across retries.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical triage with runtime team (Aditya) to confirm feasibility & performance impact
2) Draft a minimal API contract change (optional param, fallback semantics) and an SDK shim plan for our JS/TS and Python clients
3) Provide you with a target release window and a deprecation policy statement for major breaking changes

I can host a 30-min sync tomorrow with Aditya and Lauren if that works for you — propose 10:00–10:30 PT. Please confirm availability.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: API contract change for realtime callbacks - integration impact

Folks — quick technical readout after looking at acme-sdk-proposal.pdf and poking the runtime: 

- Adding an optional callback_id is low-risk if we treat it as opaque string and do not change tokenization or cache keys. The runtime already carries request_id and sequence indexes, so we'll need to ensure the callback_id isn't used for cache sharding unless explicitly requested.
- Edge cases: retries and prefix cache hits currently replay tokens without a client-supplied opaque id, so we'd need a rule: if client provides callback_id in the original request headers/params, runtime echoes it in stream; otherwise field absent. This keeps behavior deterministic for existing clients.
- SDK work: JS/TS SDK can expose onToken({token, callback_id=null, meta}) immediately as a minor bump (non-breaking). Python SDK needs the same, and we'll publish a migration note.
- Perf: negligible at scale; we should add a small binary flag to payloads to avoid any parsing overhead in hot paths.

My suggestion for partner-facing plan:
- Ship additive behavior (optional callback_id) in a minor release in ~6 weeks (target 2026-12-31 for hosted + SDK shims).
- Establish a 6-month compatibility window for any future breaking changes to streaming payloads, documented in our SDK release notes and partner SLA.
- Create a compatibility shim that maps old handler signatures to the new one for one release cycle.

Lauren — can you confirm partner engineering capacity to coordinate releases and provide a canary for Acme?

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Runtime
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

On Thu, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:05, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote: (see above)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: API contract change for realtime callbacks - integration impact

Hi Carlos — thanks for confirming availability for the sync. Recap and commitments from Redwood: 

1) Technical approach: We will accept an optional top-level string "callback_id". Behavior: 
   - If a client supplies callback_id in the request header X-Callback-Id or as a top-level request param, the runtime will echo that same value on stream messages in the callback_id field.
   - If not supplied, the field will be omitted (to preserve existing payloads).
   - The field is opaque. Runtime will not use callback_id for cache keying or routing unless explicitly toggled (we will not toggle by default).

2) Timeline: 
   - Target minor release for hosted API + JS/TS SDK shim: 2026-12-31 (public beta)
   - SDK stable release (JS/Python) with migration notes: 2027-01-31
   - Deprecation policy: Redwood will provide a minimum 6-month notice before any breaking streaming payload changes. Any breaking change will be coordinated via partner channels and our SDK release notes.

3) Partner support: Lauren will provide a canary deployment for Acme and a partner-runbook with sample code (JS + Python) showing handler migration. Aditya's team will add the binary flag to avoid perf regressions.

4) Action items (owners):
   - Aditya: finalize runtime echo and perf flag, open a GitHub issue with spec (target: 2026-11-24)
   - Lauren: schedule canary + partner runbook, prepare release notes draft (target: 2026-12-10)
   - Monica: confirm Acme's gated customers list and document the integration test cases.

Attached: a draft API contract patch for your review (acme-sdk-proposal.pdf) and our internal compat matrix (compat-matrix.csv). Also linking the GitHub issue where we'll track progress: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1427

Would you like us to go ahead and open a private repo for the canary artifacts and early builds? We can give Acme an org-level invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in for your 3.0 target.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
